title: 509.  America in '68: The Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr. (Part 2)

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, I'm only going to talk to you just for a minute or so this evening, because I have some very sad news for all of you.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，今晚我只占用大家一分钟左右的时间，因为我有一个非常悲痛的消息要告诉你们。

sentences.en: And I think sad news for all of our fellow citizens and people who love peace all over the world.
sentences.zh: 我想这对我们所有的同胞，以及全世界热爱和平的人们来说，都是一个悲痛的消息。

sentences.en: And that is that Martin Luther King was shot and was killed tonight in Memphis, Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金今晚在田纳西州孟菲斯市遭枪击身亡。

sentences.en: Martin Luther King dedicated his life to love and to justice between fellow human beings.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金一生致力于人类之间的爱与正义。

sentences.en: He died in the cause of that effort.
sentences.zh: 他为这一事业献出了生命。

sentences.en: In this difficult day, in this difficult time for the United States, it's perhaps well to ask what kind of a nation we are and what direction we want to move in.
sentences.zh: 在这个艰难的日子里，在这个对美国而言艰难的时刻，或许我们应该扪心自问：我们是一个什么样的国家？我们想要走向何方？

sentences.en: And for those of you who are black, you can be filled with bitterness and with hatred and a desire for revenge.
sentences.zh: 对于你们中的黑人同胞，你们可能会充满愤懑、仇恨和复仇的渴望。

sentences.en: We can move in that direction as a country in greater polarization.
sentences.zh: 我们可以作为一个国家，在更大的两极分化中走向那个方向。

sentences.en: Black people amongst blacks and white amongst whites filled with hatred toward one another.
sentences.zh: 黑人对黑人，白人对白人，彼此心中充满仇恨。

sentences.en: Or we can make an effort, as Martin Luther King did, to understand and to comprehend and replace that violence,
sentences.zh: 或者，我们可以像马丁·路德·金那样，努力去理解、去包容，并用这种努力去取代暴力，

sentences.en: that stain of bloodshed that has spread across our land with an effort to understand compassion and love.
sentences.zh: 取代那片蔓延在我们国土上的血腥污点，转而以理解、同情和爱来代替。

sentences.en: So that was Robert F.
sentences.zh: 以上就是罗伯特·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy on the 4th of April 1968, speaking to a crowd in Indianapolis, a crowd that was largely black and who, when Bobby Kennedy stood up to give that speech,
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪在1968年4月4日对印第安纳波利斯一群听众的讲话，那群听众大多是黑人，而当鲍比·肯尼迪站起来发表那次演讲时，

sentences.en: didn't know that Martin Luther King had been shot.
sentences.zh: 他们还不知道马丁·路德·金已经遇刺了。

sentences.en: So at the beginning of that interview, you listen to it, you can hear, I assume, Kennedy's aides in the background kind of talking about, do they know, do people know,
sentences.zh: 所以在那段采访的开头，如果你仔细听，我想你能听到肯尼迪的助手们在背景里谈论着，他们知道吗？人们知道吗？

sentences.en: what's the news?
sentences.zh: 消息是什么？

sentences.en: And then he stands up and it's completely extemporized, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 然后他站了起来，这完全是即兴发挥的，不是吗？

sentences.en: So it's an amazing speech under the circumstances.
sentences.zh: 所以在当时的情况下，这真是一场了不起的演讲。

sentences.en: And of course, what enhances the sense of drama and tragedy about it is, of course,
sentences.zh: 当然，让这场演讲更具戏剧性和悲剧色彩的，自然是，

sentences.en: that Bobby Kennedy himself is the brother of a man who had been assassinated and in due course will himself go on to be shot.
sentences.zh: 鲍比·肯尼迪本人就是一位被暗杀者的兄弟，而他自己最终也难逃被枪杀的命运。

sentences.en: Yeah, agreed.
sentences.zh: 是的，同意。

sentences.en: So you did two versions of that, didn't you, of that speech?
sentences.zh: 所以你做了两个版本的演讲，对吧？

sentences.en: And the second one I thought was pretty good.
sentences.zh: 我觉得第二个版本相当不错。

sentences.en: The warm-up is a kind of cross between the Kaiser and Bugs Bunny.
sentences.zh: 热身部分听起来像是德皇和兔八哥的结合体。

sentences.en: Yeah, I felt it didn't adequately convey the sense of tragedy and pathos that I genuinely want to, because this is actually, I mean, as I say, a very,
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得它没能充分传达出我真心想要表达的那种悲剧感和凄凉感，因为这实际上，我是说，正如我所说，是一场非常，

sentences.en: very moving and powerful speech.
sentences.zh: 非常动人且有力的演讲。

sentences.en: It is, totally.
sentences.zh: 确实，完全是这样。

sentences.en: I hope that I have done it sufficient justice that people get some sense of that.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能给予它足够的尊重，让人们能感受到这一点。

sentences.en: I think your version was really good, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你的版本真的很棒，汤姆。

sentences.en: I'm not going to stamp on it.
sentences.zh: 我不会去画蛇添足的。

sentences.en: That's very kind of you.
sentences.zh: 你太客气了。

sentences.en: I am going to say that if listeners want to go on YouTube, they can hear the speech.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，如果听众想去YouTube上听听，他们可以找到这段演讲。

sentences.en: And it is very, very moving to hear the electricity in the air, the shock of the crowd, Kennedy's kind of reedy voice.
sentences.zh: 听到空气中那种紧张的电流感，人群的震惊，以及肯尼迪那种略带沙哑的声音，真的非常、非常感人。

sentences.en: Rawness.
sentences.zh: 原始感。

sentences.en: Yeah, rawness.
sentences.zh: 是的，原始感。

sentences.en: The rawness of it.
sentences.zh: 那种原始的震撼。

sentences.en: And am I right that this is almost the only time he ever talks in public about the assassination of his brother, JFK?
sentences.zh: 我没记错的话，这几乎是他唯一一次在公开场合谈论他哥哥肯尼迪总统的遇刺事件，对吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We'll come on to the second part of the speech in our next episode.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下一集讨论演讲的第二部分。

sentences.en: But you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 但你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: It's one of the only times really where he lays himself bare in that way in front of a crowd at a moment that is so charged with tension, because as you say,
sentences.zh: 这确实是他为数不多在如此紧张的时刻，在人群面前如此袒露心迹的场合，因为正如你所说，

sentences.en: the crowd is largely black in Indianapolis.
sentences.zh: 在印第安纳波利斯，人群主要是黑人。

sentences.en: So, we ended the last episode with Lynch and Johnson pulling out of the presidential race.
sentences.zh: 所以，上一集我们讲到林奇和约翰逊退出了总统竞选。

sentences.en: Kennedy has only been in the campaign for a few days.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪加入竞选才几天。

sentences.en: So, we are now, what, five days after Johnson pulled out?
sentences.zh: 所以，现在距离约翰逊退选已经过去，嗯，五天了？

sentences.en: And we have that sense now of events piling on events.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有一种事件接踵而至的感觉。

sentences.en: So, today's episode is all about Martin Luther King, his final days, and his assassination, one of the most tragic moments in American history.
sentences.zh: 所以，今天这一集的主题是马丁·路德·金，他最后的日子，以及他的遇刺，这是美国历史上最悲剧的时刻之一。

sentences.en: So, perhaps we should set the scene a bit, because we have had Martin Luther King on the podcast before.
sentences.zh: 那么，也许我们应该先交代一下背景，因为我们之前在播客里讲过马丁·路德·金。

sentences.en: Some listeners may remember we did that episode about his I Have a Dream speech.
sentences.zh: 有些听众可能记得我们做过关于他《我有一个梦想》演讲的那一集。

sentences.en: We did it on location, didn't we, in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们是在华盛顿现场录制的，对吧？

sentences.en: So, we ended that episode.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们结束了那一集。

sentences.en: It's kind of King's high point.
sentences.zh: 那是金的人生巅峰。

sentences.en: King was one of the most admired men on the planet.
sentences.zh: 金是这个星球上最受敬仰的人之一。

sentences.en: In 1964, Americans named him their fourth most admired man in the world, behind President Johnson, Winston Churchill, and President Eisenhower.
sentences.zh: 1964年，美国人将他评为世界上第四受敬仰的人，排在约翰逊总统、温斯顿·丘吉尔和艾森豪威尔总统之后。

sentences.en: Interestingly, if you track him, King's popularity very obviously declines in the next few years.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，如果你追踪他的数据，金的受欢迎程度在接下来的几年里明显下降了。

sentences.en: So, by 1966, he had fallen off the list entirely.
sentences.zh: 到了1966年，他已经完全跌出了榜单。

sentences.en: And actually, the Gallup poll showed that six out of ten Americans now viewed King unfavorably.
sentences.zh: 事实上，盖洛普民意调查显示，十分之六的美国人当时对金持负面看法。

sentences.en: Now, given that he's now a secular saint, Martin Luther King Day and so on, a lot of people may find that surprising.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他现在是一位世俗圣人，有马丁·路德·金纪念日等等，很多人可能会觉得这很惊讶。

sentences.en: How could people view him unfavorably?
sentences.zh: 人们怎么会对他持负面看法呢？

sentences.en: And it's a complicated story, but one reason for it is that having previously had his civil rights campaign in the South.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的故事，但原因之一是，他之前在南方开展了民权运动。

sentences.en: So, King is, of course, a Baptist minister.
sentences.zh: 金当然是一位浸信会牧师。

sentences.en: He's from Atlanta, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 他来自佐治亚州的亚特兰大。

sentences.en: He spent so much of his time in Alabama, in Mississippi, in Georgia, and so on.
sentences.zh: 他把大量时间花在了阿拉巴马州、密西西比州、佐治亚州等地。

sentences.en: But now he's been moving to the North.
sentences.zh: 但现在他开始向北方转移。

sentences.en: So, he and other activists are conscious that actually there are, you know, enormous numbers of African Americans in the great cities of the North.
sentences.zh: 所以，他和其它活动人士意识到，实际上，在北方的大城市里有大量的非裔美国人。

sentences.en: They'd moved there in the first half of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 他们在20世纪上半叶搬到了那里。

sentences.en: And their plight, that they're not subject to de jure segregation as they are in the South.
sentences.zh: 他们的困境在于，他们不像在南方那样受到法律上的种族隔离。

sentences.en: You know, their lives aren't brilliant either.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们的生活也不怎么样。

sentences.en: They are much more likely than their white neighbors to be unemployed, subject to sort of informal discrimination, as we're of various kinds.
sentences.zh: 他们比白人邻居更有可能失业，受到各种非正式的歧视。

sentences.en: Housing discrimination and so on, their schools in black areas tend to be less well-funded than white schools.
sentences.zh: 住房歧视等等，黑人社区的学校往往比白人学校资金更匮乏。

sentences.en: They suffer police brutality, all of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他们遭受警察暴力，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And the implication of that, presumably, is unsettling for everyone in the United States.
sentences.zh: 而这带来的影响，想必对美国的所有人来说都是令人不安的。

sentences.en: Because it implies that racial prejudice isn't just something that is legislated for, or a legacy of the South or the Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 因为它暗示种族偏见不仅仅是法律规定的，也不仅仅是南方或邦联的遗产。

sentences.en: That it is something that is a poison within the entire fabric of the United States, North as well as South.
sentences.zh: 它是美国整个社会结构中的毒素，无论北方还是南方。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: And when King does go North, so he went North in the summer of 1966 to Chicago, and he tries to dramatize this, as he had dramatized the discrimination in the Deep South,
sentences.zh: 当金真的北上时，他在1966年夏天去了芝加哥，他试图让这种歧视戏剧化，就像他在深南地区所做的那样，

sentences.en: it doesn't really work.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有真正奏效。

sentences.en: So, he campaigns against housing segregation in the streets of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 他在芝加哥街头开展反对住房隔离的运动。

sentences.en: His march is the subject of intense violence, intense hostility from working class, blue-collar, kind of white Chicagoans, also from the city authorities who are Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他的游行遭到了芝加哥工人阶级、蓝领白人的强烈暴力和敌意，也遭到了民主党领导的市政府的敌视。

sentences.en: They give him no cooperation at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不配合他。

sentences.en: The local press accuse him of being in league with kind of organized crime to create confusion and turbulence and to compound danger to Chicagoans.
sentences.zh: 当地媒体指责他与有组织犯罪勾结，制造混乱和动荡，加剧了芝加哥人的危险。

sentences.en: And King actually comes back from Chicago and he says, my goodness, this is worse than anything I'd ever faced in the South.
sentences.zh: 金从芝加哥回来后说，天哪，这比我在南方遇到的任何事情都要糟糕。

sentences.en: It is more entrenched, more vicious, partly because it's not a question, as you said, Tom, it's not a question of kind of the legacy of slavery and laws.
sentences.zh: 它更加根深蒂固，更加恶毒，部分原因正如你所说，汤姆，这不仅仅是奴隶制遗产和法律的问题。

sentences.en: Because it is in people's imaginations.
sentences.zh: 因为它存在于人们的想象中。

sentences.en: It is intangible, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，它是无形的。

sentences.en: Mind-forged manacles.
sentences.zh: 思想铸就的枷锁。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's a sense, I think, as well, that he's very discomforted by the rightward turn in American politics more generally.
sentences.zh: 我想，他对于美国政治更广泛地向右转也感到非常不安。

sentences.en: So, the big gains for the Republicans in the 1966 midterms about law and order.
sentences.zh: 所以，共和党在1966年中期选举中大获全胜，打的是法律与秩序的旗号。

sentences.en: Journalists start saying to him, come on, are you still going on about this?
sentences.zh: 记者开始问他，得了吧，你还要继续谈论这个吗？

sentences.en: So, there's a famous exchange with CBS's Mike Wallace who says, don't you find that the American people are getting a little tired, truly, of this whole civil rights struggle?
sentences.zh: 所以，CBS的迈克·华莱士曾有一段著名的对话，他说，难道你不觉得美国人民真的对整个民权斗争感到有点厌倦了吗？

sentences.en: King finds this clearly very demoralizing.
sentences.zh: 金显然觉得这非常令人沮丧。

sentences.en: He finds it hard to raise money.
sentences.zh: 他发现筹款变得很困难。

sentences.en: His staff are becoming exhausted, kind of fractious, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他的员工变得精疲力竭，变得急躁，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Can I also just ask you, you mentioned the Republican gains in 1966 and said that this is focused on law and order.
sentences.zh: 我能问一下吗，你提到了1966年共和党的胜利，并说这集中在法律与秩序上。

sentences.en: And it's a theme throughout the 60s, isn't it, that law and order is a bit of a dog whistle.
sentences.zh: 这是一个贯穿60年代的主题，不是吗？法律与秩序有点像是一种政治暗语。

sentences.en: That it is a way for white politicians to stoke racial anxieties among white voters without actually being overtly raciSt.
sentences.zh: 这是白人政客在不公开表现出种族主义的情况下，煽动白人选民种族焦虑的一种方式。

sentences.en: Is that fair or not fair?
sentences.zh: 这种说法公平吗？

sentences.en: Both.
sentences.zh: 两者皆有。

sentences.en: That's a very evasive answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常回避的回答。

sentences.en: So, I think it's perfectly reasonable to be very anxious about crime because crime has been shooting up so much.
sentences.zh: 我认为，对犯罪感到非常焦虑是完全合理的，因为犯罪率一直在飙升。

sentences.en: But I think there is also a degree to which it is also a dog whistle.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在某种程度上，它确实也是一种政治暗语。

sentences.en: And we will do two episodes in this series on George Wallace and Richard Nixon where we'll really explore that because, of course,
sentences.zh: 我们将在本系列中专门用两集来讨论乔治·华莱士和理查德·尼克松，届时我们将深入探讨这一点，因为当然，

sentences.en: both of them really go for the law and order issue.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都非常热衷于法律与秩序问题。

sentences.en: So, yeah, you're right.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，你是对的。

sentences.en: And Reagan is also kind of a little bit playing with that.
sentences.zh: 里根也多多少少在利用这一点。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Reagan wins California in 66.
sentences.zh: 里根在66年赢得了加州。

sentences.en: You know, law and order is a huge part of his campaign.
sentences.zh: 你知道，法律与秩序是他竞选活动的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: So, King is already, you know, he's already, as it were, the love affair between him and the American public, such as it was, has gone sour.
sentences.zh: 所以，金已经，你知道，他已经，可以说，他和美国公众之间的蜜月期，如果曾经有过的话，已经破裂了。

sentences.en: But what makes this a lot worse is Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 但让情况变得更糟的是越南战争。

sentences.en: Vietnam is going to run through this whole 68 series.
sentences.zh: 越南战争将贯穿整个68系列。

sentences.en: It's like a poison.
sentences.zh: 它就像一种毒药。

sentences.en: King had really come out against it in 1967.
sentences.zh: 金在1967年确实公开反对它。

sentences.en: He had gone public in February 1967 at a conference.
sentences.zh: 他在1967年2月的一次会议上公开表态。

sentences.en: He had talked about this horror at the children with napalm, the broken bodies in the fields.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了对那些遭受凝固汽油弹袭击的儿童、田野里残缺不全的尸体的恐惧。

sentences.en: What are we doing?
sentences.zh: 我们在做什么？

sentences.en: Sending home half men mutilated mentally and physically.
sentences.zh: 把精神和身体都残缺不全的半个人送回家。

sentences.en: He then gave one of his greatest speeches.
sentences.zh: 随后他发表了他最伟大的演讲之一。

sentences.en: I mean, some people might say he's actually the greatest speech he ever gave.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有些人可能会说这是他发表过的最伟大的演讲。

sentences.en: April 1967 at the Riverside Church in New York.
sentences.zh: 1967年4月，在纽约河滨教堂。

sentences.en: And he talks about how he has wrestled with the issue because he knows how controversial it is.
sentences.zh: 他谈到自己是如何与这个问题作斗争的，因为他知道这有多么大的争议。

sentences.en: But he feels that as a man of the cloth, he has a duty.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得作为一名神职人员，他有责任。

sentences.en: He hasn't, he cannot stay silent any longer.
sentences.zh: 他不能再保持沉默了。

sentences.en: And he gives this magnificent denunciation of the war.
sentences.zh: 他发表了这篇对战争的宏伟谴责。

sentences.en: And he talks, you know, we have corrupted women and children.
sentences.zh: 他谈到，你知道，我们腐蚀了妇女和儿童。

sentences.en: We have killed their men.
sentences.zh: 我们杀害了他们的男人。

sentences.en: He talks about the children.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了孩子们。

sentences.en: They wander into the towns.
sentences.zh: 他们游荡在城镇里。

sentences.en: People see thousands of children homeless, without clothes, running in packs like animals.
sentences.zh: 人们看到成千上万的孩子无家可归，衣不蔽体，像动物一样成群结队地奔跑。

sentences.en: Children degraded by our soldiers as they beg for food.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在乞讨食物时受到我们士兵的羞辱。

sentences.en: Children selling their sisters to our soldiers, soliciting for their mothers.
sentences.zh: 孩子们把姐妹卖给我们的士兵，为他们的母亲拉皮条。

sentences.en: You know, it's really powerful stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的很震撼。

sentences.en: And presumably, we talked in the previous episode about how LBJ feels betrayed by progressives who've turned against him.
sentences.zh: 想必，我们在上一集谈到了林登·约翰逊是如何感到被那些背弃他的进步派所背叛的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But this is a break.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个决裂。

sentences.zh: 约翰逊和约翰逊白宫感到被金彻底背叛了，他们的关系实际上已经结束了。

sentences.en: Hanoi.

sentences.zh: 而且马丁·路德·金还有一个因素，我是说，他伟大的事业是和平抗议，难道不是吗？

sentences.en: But he has, coming up on his kind of left wing, I guess, his left flank.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎在左翼，或者说左翼侧翼，面临着某种压力。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.

sentences.en: Because, of course, when they organised all those marches in the South, they knew, they
sentences.zh: 因为当然，当他们在南方组织所有那些游行时，他们很清楚，他们

sentences.en: bargained for the fact that they would be attacked, that they would be mistreated by the police and the police with their dogs and all of that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们预料到自己会受到攻击，会受到警察的虐待，警察会放出警犬等等诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And they would go to prison and everything.
sentences.zh: 他们会坐牢，会经历这一切。

sentences.zh: 他们会公开受苦。

sentences.zh: 你知道，非暴力，在别人攻击你时公开受苦，是他们战略中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: I mean, Martin Luther King obviously is, as you said, you know, he's a pastor.
sentences.zh: 我是说，马丁·路德·金显然正如你所说，他是一位牧师。

sentences.en: He is aware of the biblical echoes of that.
sentences.zh: 他意识到其中蕴含的圣经回响。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: The innocents who are persecuted by the apparatus of a great power.
sentences.zh: 被大国机器迫害的无辜者。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, we know what the model is there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都知道那是怎样的模式。

sentences.en: But what you have from about 1966, 67, is not black people as suffering as the people who are being subjected to violence.
sentences.zh: 但从1966、67年左右开始，你看到的不再是黑人作为遭受暴力的人在受苦。

sentences.en: But in the newspapers now, you have stories about African-Americans who are carrying out violence.
sentences.zh: 报纸上开始出现关于非裔美国人实施暴力的报道。

sentences.en: So most obviously the rioters in the cities in 66, 67.
sentences.zh: 最明显的例子就是66、67年城市里的暴乱者。

sentences.en: But also, you have younger activists now who say, we have suffered enough.
sentences.zh: 但同时，也有一些年轻的活动家说，我们已经受够了。

sentences.en: You know, the time for just meekly marching is over.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种温顺游行的时代已经结束了。

sentences.en: And so Malcolm X.
sentences.zh: 所以马尔科姆·X……

sentences.en: Well, Malcolm X has already been shot at this point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，马尔科姆·X此时已经被枪杀了。

sentences.en: But Malcolm X is, of course, a trailblazer, a harbinger for this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但马尔科姆·X当然是这种思潮的先驱和预兆。

sentences.zh: “黑人力量”这个口号来自一个叫斯托克利·卡迈克尔的人，他是一位年轻得多的活动家。

sentences.en: He is on a march through the South in the summer of 1966, and he starts chanting black power, black power.
sentences.zh: 1966年夏天，他在南方游行时，开始高呼“黑人力量，黑人力量”。

sentences.en: And younger, more militant activists are like, at laSt.
sentences.zh: 而那些更年轻、更激进的活动家们觉得：终于来了。

sentences.en: And they say, finally, you know, somebody who's got a bit of backbone will stand up to the white establishment.

sentences.en: And also, they're quite cool, aren't they?

sentences.zh: 我是说，还有汤姆·沃尔夫提到的那些“激进时尚”的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The white liberals as well, you know, they find it quite edgy and, yeah, bringing them along to dinner parties and things.
sentences.zh: 白人自由派也是，你知道，他们觉得这很前卫，还会把他们带到晚宴上之类的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 所以，黑豹党在1967年春天真正爆发了。

sentences.zh: 像鲍比·希尔和休伊·牛顿这样的人，他们武装入侵了加利福尼亚州的首府萨克拉门托。

sentences.en: Huey Newton said, and I quote, political power comes to the barrel of a gun.
sentences.zh: 休伊·牛顿曾说，引用他的话：“政治权力来自枪杆子。”

sentences.en: We do not believe in passive and nonviolent tactics.
sentences.zh: 我们不相信消极和非暴力的策略。

sentences.en: They haven't worked for us black people.
sentences.zh: 这对我们黑人来说根本行不通。

sentences.en: They are bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 它们已经破产了。

sentences.en: And do you think that, I mean, in the 60s, things are cool and you have to constantly be moving.
sentences.zh: 你觉得，我是说，在60年代，事情很酷，你必须不断前进。

sentences.en: You need new things, by definition.
sentences.zh: 根据定义，你需要新鲜事物。

sentences.en: If you stay with the old tried ways of doing things, you know, you're basically Cliff Richard.
sentences.zh: 如果你固守那些老旧的行事方式，你知道，你基本上就是克里夫·理查德（那种老派人物）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 你是个老古板。

sentences.en: You're square.
sentences.zh: 你是个老古板。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 我是说，这也是当时气候的一部分吗？

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I absolutely think it is.
sentences.zh: 我绝对认为是这样。

sentences.en: So, the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, SNCC, as it is called, which has been such a big part of the civil rights movement in the South.
sentences.zh: 所以，学生非暴力协调委员会（SNCC），作为南方民权运动的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: The name is the Nonviolent Coordinating Committee.
sentences.zh: 它的名字叫“非暴力协调委员会”。

sentences.zh: 到了1967年，它的新主席是一个叫H·拉普·布朗的人。

sentences.zh: H·拉普·布朗。

sentences.en: That's an even better name.
sentences.zh: 那名字听起来更棒。

sentences.en: He says, everybody should arm themselves and quote, wage guerrilla war on the honky white man.
sentences.zh: 他说，每个人都应该武装起来，引用他的话：“对白人种族主义者发动游击战。”

sentences.en: Let's make the Viet Cong look like Sunday school teachers.
sentences.zh: “我们要让越共看起来都像主日学校的老师。”

sentences.en: Groovy.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is exactly the kind of thing that seizes people's imagination.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这正是那种能抓住人们想象力的东西。

sentences.en: It is fashionable, frankly, in the late 1960s, and Martin Luther King is regarded as yesterday's man.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这在60年代末很时髦，而马丁·路德·金被视为“昨日黄花”。

sentences.en: Have you ever written for the New York Review of Books, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你给《纽约书评》写过稿子吗？

sentences.en: I haven't, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，我没写过。

sentences.en: Well, just as well, because they shame themselves at this point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没写也好，因为他们此时已经自取其辱了。

sentences.en: They publish an article about Martin Luther King by a guy called Andrew Copkind, August
sentences.zh: 他们在1967年8月发表了一篇关于马丁·路德·金的文章，作者叫安德鲁·科普金德。

sentences.en: King once had the ability to talk to people, the power to change them.
sentences.zh: “金曾经有能力与人对话，有改变他们的力量。”

sentences.en: But the duty of a revolutionary is to make revolutions, and King has made none.
sentences.zh: “但革命者的职责是进行革命，而金什么也没做成。”

sentences.en: He has been outstripped by his times, overtaken by events which he may have obliquely helped to produce, but could not predict.
sentences.zh: “他已经被时代抛弃，被那些他可能间接促成却无法预见的事件所超越。”

sentences.en: He is not likely to regain command.
sentences.zh: “他不太可能重新掌握主导权。”

sentences.en: Kind of, goodbye, granddad.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是说：再见，爷爷。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of like, you know, this guy hasn't kept up with Sergeant Pepper or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就像是说，这家伙没跟上《佩珀中士》的节奏之类的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's almost the same thing.

sentences.zh: 你知道，你必须跟上潮流。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The fact that he has been outpaced by his times, that the, you know, he hasn't produced results.
sentences.zh: 事实是他已经被时代淘汰了，他没有取得成果。

sentences.en: Black Americans are still likely to be poor.
sentences.zh: 美国黑人依然很可能贫穷。

sentences.en: They're still likely to go to prison.
sentences.zh: 他们依然很可能入狱。

sentences.en: All of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情。

sentences.en: We don't, you know, the time that non-violence is over, the time that urgency has begun.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要……你知道，非暴力的时代结束了，紧迫的时代开始了。

sentences.en: That's basically what people are saying.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是人们在说的。

sentences.en: And is Andrew Copkind black or white?
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·科普金德是黑人还是白人？

sentences.zh: 他是白人。

sentences.en: He's a white radical journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位白人激进记者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I mean, he's writing a bit like a white radical, it has to be said.

sentences.en: He is indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实是。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So King feels this pressure very, very deeply.
sentences.zh: 所以金感受到了这种压力，非常非常深刻。

sentences.en: If you think, he has for more than a decade, he has been in the public eye.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想，他已经在公众视野中待了十多年了。

sentences.en: He's been long days.
sentences.zh: 那是漫长的岁月。

sentences.en: He's exhausted.
sentences.zh: 他精疲力竭。

sentences.en: He's been in prison 18 times.
sentences.zh: 他坐过18次牢。

sentences.en: He has been punched in the face.
sentences.zh: 他被人打过脸。

sentences.en: He has been stabbed.
sentences.zh: 他被人捅过刀子。

sentences.en: He's been hit on the head with rocks.
sentences.zh: 他被人用石头砸过头。

sentences.en: He's been tear gassed, sprayed with water cannons, had dogs set on him.
sentences.zh: 他被催泪瓦斯熏过，被高压水枪喷过，还被放狗咬过。

sentences.en: And all the time he is traveling, he's staying in kind of cheap hotels.
sentences.zh: 而且他一直都在奔波，住的都是那种廉价旅馆。

sentences.en: This is a chilling precedent for us going on our tour of the United States, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这对我们即将开始的美国之行来说是个令人不寒而栗的先例。

sentences.en: I hope this doesn't happen to us, staying in cheap hotels.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们不会遇到这种事，住廉价旅馆。

sentences.en: We're not quite so saintly.
sentences.zh: 我们可没那么圣洁。

sentences.en: And I look at this, he's smoking and drinking too much, gaining weight, taking sleeping pills, constantly traveling, speaking and preaching.
sentences.zh: 我看着他，他抽烟喝酒太多，体重增加，服用安眠药，不断地旅行、演讲和布道。

sentences.en: This is like you on tour, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这就像你在巡演一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实是。

sentences.en: Anyway, he's under enormous stress.
sentences.zh: 总之，他承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: His marriage is also crumbling, by the way, because one of the things that people, I guess, now know about Martin Luther King is that he is a man, he's ravaged by guilt because
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他的婚姻也正在破裂，因为我想人们现在关于马丁·路德·金所知道的一件事是，他是一个人，他被内疚感折磨，因为

sentences.en: he's not perfect.

sentences.zh: 他是个罪人。

sentences.zh: 他在1967年圣诞节向妻子科雷塔坦白了一段婚外情。

sentences.zh: 她很崩溃，但并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And she was, one of the things that devastated her was that actually he was in such a mess about it.
sentences.zh: 而且，让她崩溃的一件事是，他当时对此感到如此混乱。

sentences.zh: 他看起来，引用她的话，“极其痛苦”。

sentences.en: I had not seen him like this before.
sentences.zh: “我以前从未见过他这样。”

sentences.en: And also, isn't he being hounded by the FBI and J.

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 联邦调查局对金的监视已经持续多年了。

sentences.en: J.

sentences.en: Edgar Hoover tells LBJ, tells President Johnson in the course of 1967, that he's now convinced that King is, quote, an instrument in the hands of subversive forces seeking to
sentences.zh: 他绝对痴迷于金的私生活。

sentences.en: undermine our nation.
sentences.zh: “一个有着强迫性退化性性冲动的色狼，”J·埃德加·胡佛这样评价金。

sentences.en: He is absolutely obsessed with King's love life.
sentences.zh: 他录下了金在华盛顿一家酒店与其中一位情人的对话。

sentences.en: A tomcat with obsessive degenerative sexual urges, J.
sentences.zh: 好吧，联邦调查局随后匿名将那盘录音带寄给了金的妻子，让她听。

sentences.en: Edgar Hoover says of King.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他知道。

sentences.en: He has him taped with one of his lovers in a Washington hotel.

sentences.en: Well, the FBI then sends that tape to King's wife anonymously for her to listen to.
sentences.zh: 他知道当局一直在监视他，窥探他，向报纸散布关于他的谣言。

sentences.en: So, yes, he knows.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，他承受着巨大的、巨大的道德和心理压力。

sentences.en: I mean, King is not an idiot.
sentences.zh: 而他对此的反应，实际上，很多人说，好吧，算了吧，收敛一点吧。

sentences.zh: 这让他坚持走下去。

sentences.zh: 人们在呐喊、鼓掌、欢呼和哭泣。

sentences.en: His staff who are there are standing in a kind of grim silence.
sentences.zh: 在场的随行人员则陷入了一种严峻的沉默。

sentences.en: This is awful.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Like another event in the schedule, yet more pressure.
sentences.zh: 就像日程表上的又一个活动，又多了一份压力。

sentences.en: Memphis is not a very Martin Luther King friendly town.
sentences.zh: 孟菲斯并不是一个对马丁·路德·金友好的城市。

sentences.en: This is a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 这是个坏主意。

sentences.en: However, he goes back that night to his, the usual place that he stays.
sentences.zh: 然而，那天晚上他还是回到了他通常下榻的地方。

sentences.en: And we should just talk about this because it's really important.
sentences.zh: 我们应该谈谈这件事，因为它真的很重要。

sentences.en: He stays in a motel called the Lorraine Motel.
sentences.zh: 他住在一家叫洛林汽车旅馆的地方。

sentences.en: It's in the southern end of downtown, not far from the river.
sentences.zh: 它位于市中心南端，离河边不远。

sentences.en: It's the place where it's a black family owned and blues and gospel stars when they come to Memphis always stay there.
sentences.zh: 那是一家黑人家庭拥有的旅馆，蓝调和福音音乐明星来到孟菲斯时总是住在那儿。

sentences.en: So Ray Charles has stayed there.
sentences.zh: 所以雷·查尔斯住过那里。

sentences.en: Louis Armstrong has stayed there.
sentences.zh: 路易斯·阿姆斯特朗住过那里。

sentences.en: Aretha Franklin has stayed there.
sentences.zh: 艾瑞莎·弗兰克林住过那里。

sentences.en: King has been many times and the owners let him stay for free.
sentences.zh: 金去过很多次，老板们都让他免费入住。

sentences.en: He always stays in one particular room, room 306 on the second floor.
sentences.zh: 他总是住同一个房间，二楼的306号房。

sentences.en: And if you look at photos of the motel, it's very sort of mid-60s modern, kind of mid-century modern.
sentences.zh: 如果你看那些旅馆的照片，它非常有那种60年代中期的现代感，算是世纪中叶的现代风格。

sentences.en: It's quite simple, a little bit Scandi, a bit Ikea, you could say.
sentences.zh: 它相当简洁，带点斯堪的纳维亚风格，或者说有点宜家风。

sentences.en: You know, the room with a little TV, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，房间里有台小电视，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So that's where he is.
sentences.zh: 所以他就在那儿。

sentences.en: That's where he always goes.
sentences.zh: 那是他总是去的地方。

sentences.en: Now, the next day, the next few days, he goes off to the Mississippi Delta, which is part of his Poor People's Campaign, one of the poorest places in North America.
sentences.zh: 第二天，接下来的几天，他去了密西西比三角洲，那是他“穷人运动”的一部分，也是北美最贫困的地区之一。

sentences.en: You know, the sodden cotton fields, the shacks, a place absolutely haunted by the ghosts of slavery.
sentences.zh: 你知道，泥泞的棉田，简陋的棚屋，一个绝对被奴隶制幽灵缠绕的地方。

sentences.en: So he's off in Mississippi and he's waiting to come back to Memphis for this march that he's promised.
sentences.zh: 所以他身在密西西比，等待着回到孟菲斯去履行他承诺的那场游行。

sentences.en: But there's a series of freak snowstorMs.
sentences.zh: 但却接连发生了几场罕见的暴风雪。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: Snowstorms?
sentences.zh: 暴风雪？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I didn't know they had that in the South.
sentences.zh: 我不知道南方也有这种天气。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Who knew?
sentences.zh: 谁能想到呢？

sentences.en: So there's been a lot of snow and the march is postponed and postponed and is finally rescheduled for Thursday, the 28th of March, 1968.
sentences.zh: 所以下了很多雪，游行被一推再推，最终改期到了1968年3月28日，星期四。

sentences.en: March 28, as they would say.
sentences.zh: 3月28日，正如他们所说。

sentences.en: March 28, exactly.
sentences.zh: 3月28日，没错。

sentences.en: But a spoiler alert, it will turn out very differently from what Martin Luther King is expecting.
sentences.zh: 但剧透一下，结果将与马丁·路德·金预期的截然不同。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, we will find out how, just how differently after the break.
sentences.zh: 好吧，休息之后我们会揭晓究竟有多么不同。

sentences.zh: 载有350名乘客的航班。

sentences.zh: 大博弈，英国与俄罗斯之间的战略斗争。

sentences.en: We assess our Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 我们评估我们的首相。

sentences.en: With high confidence, it was Russian.
sentences.zh: 我们有高度信心，那是俄罗斯干的。

sentences.en: Holding the Russians accountable is World War 3.
sentences.zh: 追究俄罗斯人的责任就是第三次世界大战。

sentences.en: They took down a British passenger jet containing 350 people.
sentences.zh: 他们击落了一架载有350人的英国客机。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那个人在玩火，亚历克斯。

sentences.zh: 你必须问问自己，你想玩还是不想玩？

sentences.zh: 你是首相。

sentences.zh: 你什么都没做！

sentences.zh: 我们需要了解政策背景。

sentences.zh: 今天所有相关的背景都将构建成一个框架，并分发成作战命令，即Frago。

sentences.en: A Frago that says to kill the President of Russia.
sentences.zh: 一份要求刺杀俄罗斯总统的作战命令。

sentences.zh: 一场独一无二的音频剧之旅。

sentences.en: Men like Duffy.
sentences.zh: 像达菲这样的人。

sentences.zh: 他们是我们最宝贵的武器。

sentences.zh: 被设计成一部技术严谨的地缘政治动作惊悚片。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: And we are in Memphis.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在孟菲斯。

sentences.en: It's the 28th of May, or May 28th, if you're American.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月28日，如果你是美国人的话，就是5月28日。

sentences.en: It's Thursday.
sentences.zh: 星期四。

sentences.en: And Martin Luther King, Dominic, is about to lead this much-anticipated march in aid of the trash and refuse workers through the streets of Memphis.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，马丁·路德·金即将领导这场备受期待的游行，旨在支持孟菲斯街头的环卫工人。

sentences.en: Yes, and unfortunately, the march is a complete and utter catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 是的，不幸的是，这场游行是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: For Memphis, for King himself, for the image of his campaign.
sentences.zh: 对孟菲斯，对金本人，以及对他运动的形象而言。

sentences.en: So we talked in the first half about this sense of how he'd lost control of, or was losing control of his movement.
sentences.zh: 我们在上半部分讨论过他如何失去了对运动的控制，或者说正在失去控制。

sentences.en: There's a generation gap in the movement.
sentences.zh: 运动中存在代沟。

sentences.en: There are people who are calling for greater urgency, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 有些人呼吁更强的紧迫感，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And you see this, you know, made manifest in the streets of Memphis.
sentences.zh: 你在孟菲斯的街头看到了这一点，你知道，表现得淋漓尽致。

sentences.en: Because when he gets there, he is horrified to find out that it's not the family-friendly, you know, march of women and children or whatnot,
sentences.zh: 因为当他到达那里时，他惊恐地发现，这并不是他过去在50年代末和60年代初在深南部领导的那种老少皆宜的游行。

sentences.en: that he used to lead in the Deep South, in the late 1950s and early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 那不是那种妇女儿童参与的游行。

sentences.en: There are loads of teenagers.
sentences.zh: 现场有很多青少年。

sentences.en: There are people drinking.
sentences.zh: 有人在喝酒。

sentences.en: There are people shouting about black power.
sentences.zh: 有人在呼喊“黑人权力”。

sentences.en: There were very aggressive placards about sort of taking the struggle against the whites, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 还有非常激进的标语，关于对抗白人，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And he seriously thinks, he's utterly downcast, and he seriously thinks about cancelling the march.
sentences.zh: 他认真地考虑，他感到非常沮丧，他认真考虑取消游行。

sentences.en: And then he decides, no, the best thing is probably to go ahead anyway.
sentences.zh: 然后他决定，不，最好的办法可能还是继续进行。

sentences.en: They go ahead with the march through Memphis, which is already suffering the kind of urban blights that will become such a feature of American life in the 1970s and 80s.
sentences.zh: 他们继续在孟菲斯进行游行，而这座城市已经遭受了那种在70和80年代成为美国生活特征的城市衰败。

sentences.en: So they're marching through these kind of dilapidated streets, boarded up shops, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们走过这些破败的街道，木板封住的商店，诸如此类。

sentences.en: There are a lot of pushing and shoving behind him.
sentences.zh: 他身后有很多推搡。

sentences.en: He's very conscious of this.
sentences.zh: 他对此非常敏感。

sentences.en: They get onto Beale Street, which is the home of the blues.
sentences.zh: 他们来到了比尔街，那是蓝调的发源地。

sentences.en: You know, once a great destination, now a lot of the clubs have moved out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，曾经是一个伟大的目的地，现在很多俱乐部都搬走了。

sentences.en: It feels shabby and seedy and depressing.
sentences.zh: 它感觉破旧、肮脏且令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And it's about this point that the violence starts.
sentences.zh: 就在这一点上，暴力开始了。

sentences.en: People start smashing shop windows.
sentences.zh: 人们开始砸碎商店的窗户。

sentences.en: They're looting.
sentences.zh: 他们在抢劫。

sentences.en: They're throwing bottles and bricks at the police.
sentences.zh: 他们向警察投掷瓶子和砖块。

sentences.en: The police start to wade in.
sentences.zh: 警察开始介入。

sentences.en: It all kicks off.
sentences.zh: 一切都失控了。

sentences.en: King and his allies are ushered away for their own safety by the police to a hotel, the Holiday Inn, which is a brand new high-rise luxury hotel.
sentences.zh: 金和他的盟友被警察为了安全起见护送到了一家酒店，假日酒店，那是一家全新的高层豪华酒店。

sentences.en: That's an important detail, which we'll come back to.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的细节，我们稍后会回到这一点。

sentences.en: So he's in a hotel room there and he's watching what's happening on TV and he is horrified because it is absolutely kicking off in Memphis.
sentences.zh: 所以他待在那里的酒店房间里，看着电视上发生的一切，他感到惊恐，因为孟菲斯彻底乱套了。

sentences.en: The authorities call for the National Guard.
sentences.zh: 当局要求国民警卫队出动。

sentences.en: The police chief goes on TV and he says this is a civil war.
sentences.zh: 警察局长上了电视，他说这是一场内战。

sentences.en: It's a local civil war.
sentences.zh: 这是一场地方性的内战。

sentences.en: And King, this is one of the low points in his entire life.
sentences.zh: 对金来说，这是他一生中最糟糕的时刻之一。

sentences.en: He's just standing there watching this on TV.
sentences.zh: 他只是站在那里看着电视上的这一切。

sentences.en: Because the violence is coming from the marchers as well as from the police this time.
sentences.zh: 因为这一次暴力不仅来自警察，也来自游行者。

sentences.en: So it's upended his strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以这颠覆了他的策略。

sentences.en: It has completely.
sentences.zh: 彻底颠覆了。

sentences.en: This is not, you know, Alabama policemen wading in against defenseless women and children.
sentences.zh: 这不再是阿拉巴马州的警察对手无寸铁的妇女儿童动手了。

sentences.en: These are black teenagers fighting back, looting stores, throwing things at the police.
sentences.zh: 这些是黑人青少年在反击，抢劫商店，向警察投掷东西。

sentences.en: And the sense that the violence has come from the march.
sentences.zh: 而且暴力来自游行队伍本身。

sentences.en: It's not been directed at the march.
sentences.zh: 它不是针对游行的。

sentences.en: It is the march that has created the violence.
sentences.zh: 正是游行创造了暴力。

sentences.en: And he's ringing his advisors.
sentences.zh: 他正在给他的顾问打电话。

sentences.en: He says to one of them, I know what the press will say.
sentences.zh: 他对其中一个人说，我知道媒体会怎么说。

sentences.en: They will say, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我引用一下，

sentences.en: Martin Luther King is dead.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金死了。

sentences.en: He is finished.
sentences.zh: 他完了。

sentences.en: His non-violence is nothing.
sentences.zh: 他的非暴力主张一文不值。

sentences.en: No one is listening to it.
sentences.zh: 没人听他的了。

sentences.en: And that night he can't sleep.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上他彻夜难眠。

sentences.en: He's with his greatest friend, his greatest ally, another minister called Ralph Abernathy.
sentences.zh: 他和最伟大的朋友、最亲密的盟友，另一位牧师拉尔夫·阿伯内西在一起。

sentences.en: And he says to him, you know, this country is sick.
sentences.zh: 他对他说，你知道，这个国家病了。

sentences.en: Maybe we should just give up and let it sink into its sickness.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该放弃，让它沉沦在自己的病态中。

sentences.en: Maybe violence is what people want because they're not listening to us.
sentences.zh: 也许暴力就是人们想要的，因为他们不听我们的。

sentences.en: The next day he wakes up such as he can because he's hardly had any sleep.
sentences.zh: 第二天他醒来，尽可能地醒来，因为他几乎没睡。

sentences.en: And he looks at the next day's papers and they are terrible.
sentences.zh: 他看了第二天的报纸，内容非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And part of this is because the FBI has been fueling the criticism of Martin Luther King.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是联邦调查局一直在煽动对马丁·路德·金的批评。

sentences.en: And they have told everybody, this hypocrite, this sinner, this liar and fraud.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉所有人，这个伪君子，这个罪人，这个骗子。

sentences.en: Do you know where he is?
sentences.zh: 你知道他在哪儿吗？

sentences.en: He's in a luxury hotel.
sentences.zh: 他住在一家豪华酒店里。

sentences.en: He led this march.
sentences.zh: 他领导了这场游行。

sentences.en: It all kicked off.
sentences.zh: 结果乱成一团。

sentences.en: And then he went up to his suite and he's swanning around with his friends in this fancy white owned hotel.
sentences.zh: 然后他回到套房，和朋友们在那家白人拥有的高级酒店里逍遥自在。

sentences.en: And King is devastated by this.
sentences.zh: 金对此感到崩溃。

sentences.en: And it's really important because it means that the next time he comes to Memphis, he will definitely stay at his favorite place, the Lorraine Motel.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要，因为这意味着下次他来孟菲斯时，他一定会住在他最喜欢的地方，洛林汽车旅馆。

sentences.en: No matter what the risks, because it is important to him to prove that he's not a hypocrite.
sentences.zh: 无论冒什么风险，因为向人们证明他不是伪君子对他来说很重要。

sentences.en: So on Saturday, the 30th of March, King flew back to Atlanta and he met the leaders of his kind of Southern Christian Leadership Conventional Conference or something.
sentences.zh: 所以周六，3月30日，金飞回了亚特兰大，会见了南方基督教领袖会议的领导人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they all say to him, look, that was an absolute disaster.
sentences.zh: 他们都对他说，看，那简直是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Please don't go back to Memphis, whatever you do.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，请不要再回孟菲斯了。

sentences.en: This is not, you know, your poor people's campaign is probably not a very good idea, but this Memphis trash workers business is terrible.
sentences.zh: 这不是，你知道，你的穷人运动可能不是个好主意，但这个孟菲斯环卫工人的事情太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And he is very upset at this.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到非常难过。

sentences.en: He's visibly upset.
sentences.zh: 他显然心烦意乱。

sentences.en: And he says, if I can't go to Memphis, then I can't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果我不能去孟菲斯，那我就哪儿也去不了。

sentences.en: Like, what's the point if I can't go somewhere like that and stand up for these people?
sentences.zh: 就像是，如果我不能去那种地方为这些人挺身而出，那还有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: They still don't agree.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然不同意。

sentences.en: And he actually does something he's never really done before.
sentences.zh: 于是他做了一件他以前从未真正做过的事。

sentences.en: He storms out in a fury.
sentences.zh: 他怒气冲冲地离开了。

sentences.en: Biographers have poured over the details of that afternoon.
sentences.zh: 传记作家们仔细研究了那天下午的每一个细节。

sentences.en: What, where did he go?
sentences.zh: 他到底去了哪里？

sentences.en: Did he go to see his father?
sentences.zh: 他是去见他父亲了吗？

sentences.en: Did he go to see one of his lovers?
sentences.zh: 他是去见他的情人了吗？

sentences.en: Did he just go and pray?
sentences.zh: 还是他只是去祈祷了？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不得而知。

sentences.en: But in his absence, all the other people, a lot of whom, of course, are ministers too, are so shocked and upset that he has stormed out.
sentences.zh: 但在他离开期间，其他所有人都——当然其中许多人也是牧师——对他的愤然离去感到非常震惊和不安。

sentences.en: They say, we will do anything to bring him back and to please him.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们愿意做任何事来让他回来，让他消气。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: We will make this work.
sentences.zh: 我们会促成这件事。

sentences.en: We'll go with this poor people's campaign and we'll go with the Memphis thing.
sentences.zh: 我们会支持这次穷人运动，也会支持孟菲斯的行动。

sentences.en: So he comes back and he is delighted by this.
sentences.zh: 于是他回来了，并对此感到非常高兴。

sentences.zh: 但当然，金毕竟是金，汤姆，他的日程表让你自己的日程表看起来就像是一片空白，什么都没发生过，

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because he's got incredibly heavy stubble.
sentences.zh: 因为他的胡茬特别硬。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: And only this sort of chemical that he puts on his face will get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 只有这种他涂在脸上的化学制剂才能除掉它。

sentences.en: It's called magic shaving powder, which is so American.
sentences.zh: 这叫神奇剃须粉，非常有美国特色。

sentences.en: I mean, what?
sentences.zh: 我是说，什么鬼？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: And doubtless a lawsuit is brought against the manufacturers three years later.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，三年后这家制造商肯定被起诉了。

sentences.en: By the way, if you're from the magic shaving powder company, please sue Tom and not me.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你是神奇剃须粉公司的，请去起诉汤姆，别起诉我。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Apologize for that.
sentences.zh: 为那句话道歉。

sentences.en: So they're now running late and they have to go for dinner.
sentences.zh: 他们现在迟到了，得去吃晚饭了。

sentences.en: He changes his shirt.
sentences.zh: 他换了件衬衫。

sentences.en: He's put on weight.
sentences.zh: 他长胖了。

sentences.en: We said how unhealthy he was in his lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 我们之前说过他的生活方式有多不健康。

sentences.en: So he's actually too fat for the first shirt that he puts on.
sentences.zh: 所以他穿的第一件衬衫其实已经太紧了。

sentences.en: He gets his tie.
sentences.zh: 他拿了领带。

sentences.en: He goes all this.
sentences.zh: 他做了这一切。

sentences.en: He goes out on the balcony of 555.
sentences.zh: 他走到了555号房间的阳台上。

sentences.en: Ralph Abernathy is still getting ready.
sentences.zh: 拉尔夫·阿伯内西还在准备。

sentences.en: So this is the scene.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时的场景。

sentences.en: This low slung motel just on the edge of downtown Memphis.
sentences.zh: 这家低矮的汽车旅馆就在孟菲斯市中心边缘。

sentences.en: He's standing there on the balcony for all to see in front of room 306.
sentences.zh: 他站在306号房间前的阳台上，所有人都能看见他。

sentences.en: The motel, by the way, has been featured in local news reports about him being in Memphis.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，这家汽车旅馆曾出现在当地关于他身在孟菲斯的新闻报道中。

sentences.en: Everyone knows he's there.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道他在那儿。

sentences.en: So everyone knows he's there.
sentences.zh: 所以大家都知道他在那儿。

sentences.en: And the TV news pictures showed the room and the room number.
sentences.zh: 电视新闻画面显示了房间和房号。

sentences.en: So everybody knows he is there.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都知道他在那儿。

sentences.en: There are police observers in a kind of firehouse on the other side of the street who have been watching him all this time.
sentences.zh: 街对面有个消防站，里面有警察观察员，他们一直盯着他。

sentences.en: One of them says at this point, there is Dr. King right there.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人这时说，金博士就在那儿。

sentences.en: I presume he's going to supper.
sentences.zh: 我想他要去吃晚饭了。

sentences.en: He's there for a couple of minutes.
sentences.zh: 他在那儿待了几分钟。

sentences.en: It's now 557 or so.
sentences.zh: 现在大约是5点57分。

sentences.en: He goes inside to get his suit jacket.
sentences.zh: 他走进房间去拿西装外套。

sentences.en: He puts it on.
sentences.zh: 他穿上了外套。

sentences.en: In the pockets, there's a note that he's writing for a speech that he's going to give.
sentences.zh: 口袋里有一张纸条，是他为即将发表的演讲写的草稿。

sentences.en: And the line that is written is, nothing is gained without sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：没有牺牲，就一无所获。

sentences.en: He comes back out to the balcony.
sentences.zh: 他回到阳台上。

sentences.en: He's got his jacket on now.
sentences.zh: 他现在穿上了外套。

sentences.en: His driver is downstairs with his Cadillac.
sentences.zh: 他的司机正开着凯迪拉克在楼下等候。

sentences.en: And also downstairs are a group of other younger civil rights leaders, most notable of whom is Jesse Jackson,
sentences.zh: 楼下还有一群年轻的民权领袖，其中最著名的是杰西·杰克逊，

sentences.en: with whom Martin Luther King has had a slightly turbulent relationship.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金与他的关系曾有些动荡。

sentences.en: They've had a bit of a falling out.
sentences.zh: 他们闹过一点不愉快。

sentences.en: A very prominent political figure in the 80s, weren't he?
sentences.zh: 他在80年代是个非常显赫的政治人物，不是吗？

sentences.en: Very prominent, exactly.
sentences.zh: 非常显赫，没错。

sentences.en: The most prominent black leader in the 1980s and 1990s.
sentences.zh: 他是80和90年代最著名的黑人领袖。

sentences.en: And Jackson shouts out to him, our leader.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊对他喊道：我们的领袖。

sentences.en: And King says, ah, Jesse, I want you to come to dinner tonight.
sentences.zh: 金说：啊，杰西，我想让你今晚也来吃晚饭。

sentences.en: And this is a nice moment because it's a bit of reconciliation after the arguments they've had about civil rights strategy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美好的时刻，因为在他们就民权策略发生争执后，这算是一种和解。

sentences.en: It's now just gone past six o'clock.
sentences.zh: 现在刚过六点。

sentences.en: Jackson says, I've got this guy here who's a saxophoniSt.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊说：我这儿有个人，是个萨克斯手。

sentences.en: He's called Ben Branch.
sentences.zh: 他叫本·布兰奇。

sentences.en: He's going to be doing a concert.
sentences.zh: 他要举办一场音乐会。

sentences.en: He's going to be playing for the sanitation workers at the temple.
sentences.zh: 他要在教堂为环卫工人们演奏。

sentences.en: And King says, Ben, I want you to do this song.
sentences.zh: 金说：本，我想让你演奏这首歌。

sentences.en: Take my hand, precious Lord.
sentences.zh: 《牵着我的手，亲爱的主》。

sentences.en: Sing it real pretty.
sentences.zh: 唱得好听点。

sentences.en: And the guy says, I sure will, Doc.
sentences.zh: 那人说：我一定会的，博士。

sentences.en: And then the driver gets out, Solomon Jones, he gets out of the car and he shouts up to King.
sentences.zh: 然后司机所罗门·琼斯下了车，他冲着金喊道。

sentences.en: He says, it's getting chilly.
sentences.zh: 他说：天变冷了。

sentences.en: I think you're going to need a top coat.
sentences.zh: 我想你需要一件外套。

sentences.en: They're so solicitous about him.
sentences.zh: 他们对他真是关怀备至。

sentences.en: They're so protective of him.
sentences.zh: 他们对他保护得太好了。

sentences.en: You know, he means so much to these people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他对这些人意义重大。

sentences.en: And King says the last words he ever says.
sentences.zh: 金说了他人生中最后的话。

sentences.en: Okay, Jonesy, you really know how to take good care of me.
sentences.zh: 好的，琼斯，你真的很会照顾我。

sentences.en: And then he gets a menthol cigarette out of his pocket and he turns back from the railing to go back to his room to get this overcoat.
sentences.zh: 然后他从口袋里掏出一支薄荷香烟，转身离开栏杆，准备回房间去拿外套。

sentences.en: And it's then that a single shot rings out, deafening sound.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一声枪响，震耳欲聋。

sentences.en: Immediately, everybody there knew that King had been shot.
sentences.zh: 在场的所有人立刻意识到金中枪了。

sentences.en: The parking lot is full of people screaming and shouting, get an ambulance, get an ambulance.
sentences.zh: 停车场里到处是尖叫和呼喊声：叫救护车，快叫救护车。

sentences.en: Oh my God, they've shot him.
sentences.zh: 天哪，他们开枪打中他了。

sentences.en: Don't move him and all of this.
sentences.zh: 别动他，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: The co-owner of the motel, who's a woman called Lurie Bailey, at this point had a stroke, fell into a coma and later died.
sentences.zh: 汽车旅馆的共同所有人，一位叫卢里·贝利的女士，当时中风了，陷入昏迷，后来去世了。

sentences.en: Nobody talked about her, but she died at the same time.
sentences.zh: 没人提起她，但她是在同一时间去世的。

sentences.en: On the balcony, they rush up.
sentences.zh: 人们冲上阳台。

sentences.en: King is down.
sentences.zh: 金倒下了。

sentences.en: He has been hit on the right side of his jaw by a bullet, soft bullet that has expanded and has then ripped into his neck.
sentences.zh: 他的右下颚被一颗子弹击中，那是一颗膨胀弹，击中后撕裂了他的脖子。

sentences.en: There's massive bleeding.
sentences.zh: 流血非常严重。

sentences.en: He's immediately in shock.
sentences.zh: 他立刻陷入了休克。

sentences.en: His pulse is fading straight away.
sentences.zh: 他的脉搏瞬间消失了。

sentences.en: They rushed him to the nearest hospital, which was St. Joseph's Hospital.
sentences.zh: 他们把他紧急送往最近的医院，即圣约瑟夫医院。

sentences.en: He was at this point barely alive.
sentences.zh: 当时他已几乎没有生命迹象。

sentences.en: He had effectively been killed almost instantly.
sentences.zh: 他实际上几乎是瞬间死亡的。

sentences.en: I mean, very JFK, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这和肯尼迪遇刺非常像，不是吗？

sentences.en: The wound to the head.
sentences.zh: 头部中弹。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The absolutely clearly fatal injury and people trying to resuscitate what can't be resuscitated.
sentences.zh: 绝对致命的伤口，人们试图抢救那些无法挽回的生命。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: 20 minutes after this moment, Jesse Jackson rings Coretta, his wife, in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 事发20分钟后，杰西·杰克逊给他在亚特兰大的妻子科雷塔打了电话。

sentences.en: She's been out shopping with her daughter.
sentences.zh: 她当时正和女儿在外购物。

sentences.en: At the same point, while Jackson's on the phone saying there's an accident, he's been hit on the shoulder so Jackson doesn't tell her the whole truth straight away.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，杰克逊在电话里说发生了事故，他只是肩膀中弹，所以杰克逊没有立刻告诉她全部真相。

sentences.en: His boys, who are watching TV, see a newsflash about their father and they run into their mother to tell her.
sentences.zh: 他的孩子们正在看电视，看到了关于他们父亲的新闻快讯，于是跑去告诉母亲。

sentences.en: At this point, the surgeons are just about to get ready, working on King.
sentences.zh: 此时，外科医生正准备对金进行手术。

sentences.en: Right away, the chief neurosurgeon says to Ralph Abernafi, it will be a blessing if he dies.
sentences.zh: 神经外科主任立刻对拉尔夫·阿伯内西说，如果他死了，那反而是种解脱。

sentences.en: He has been so badly injured, he would have suffered a horrendous brain damage.
sentences.zh: 他伤得太重了，即便活下来也会遭受可怕的脑损伤。

sentences.en: His spine is cut and he has sustained awful brain damage.
sentences.zh: 他的脊椎断了，大脑也受到了严重的损伤。

sentences.en: And actually, the whole thing is done and dusted very quickly.
sentences.zh: 事实上，整个过程很快就结束了。

sentences.en: At five minutes past seven, he is pronounced dead.
sentences.zh: 七点零五分，他被宣告死亡。

sentences.en: His parents are listening in their local church in Atlanta, the Ebenezer Baptist Church, King's Home Church.
sentences.zh: 他的父母正在亚特兰大的当地教堂，也就是金的母会——埃比尼泽浸信会教堂听礼拜。

sentences.en: They're listening to the radio if it's a really, really sort of heart-rending scene and they hear the news reports of their son has died.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在听收音机，那是一个非常非常令人心碎的场景，他们听到了儿子去世的新闻报道。

sentences.en: Now, what about the killer?
sentences.zh: 那么，凶手呢？

sentences.en: Within moments, the police, who of course are there, right?
sentences.zh: 片刻之内，警察就到了，他们当然就在那儿，对吧？

sentences.en: They're spying on King.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在监视金。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They are on the scene.
sentences.zh: 他们就在现场。

sentences.en: In the chaos, in the car park of the motel, they're like, where did the shot come from?
sentences.zh: 在混乱中，在汽车旅馆的停车场里，他们都在问，枪声是从哪儿来的？

sentences.en: All of King's friends point the same way.
sentences.zh: 金博士所有的朋友都指向同一个方向。

sentences.en: To this particular kind of run-down looking brick house on South Main Street.
sentences.zh: 指向南大街上一栋看起来破破烂烂的砖房。

sentences.en: So this was a boarding house run by a woman called Bessie Brewer.
sentences.zh: 那是一间由贝西·布鲁尔经营的寄宿公寓。

sentences.en: Americans would call it, I think, a rooming house or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我想美国人会称之为出租屋之类的吧。

sentences.en: Hampton Sides wrote a brilliant book on the whole story about King's killer and the manhunt for him.
sentences.zh: 汉普顿·赛兹写过一本精彩的书，讲述了金博士遇刺及随后搜捕凶手的全过程。

sentences.en: And he says it was a haven for invalids, derelicts, transients, riverboat workers and small-time crooks.
sentences.zh: 他说那里曾是残疾人、流浪汉、过路客、内河船员和三流罪犯的避难所。

sentences.en: The police basically pile into this house.
sentences.zh: 警察基本上是一窝蜂地冲进了这栋房子。

sentences.en: And Dominic, can I just ask, the police, is this the local police force or is this the FBI?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我能问一下吗，这些警察是当地警局的，还是联邦调查局（FBI）的？

sentences.en: It's the local police.
sentences.zh: 是当地警察。

sentences.en: It's the local police because it's the local police who are on the scene.
sentences.zh: 是当地警察，因为当时在现场的就是他们。

sentences.en: But the FBI get involved almost immediately.
sentences.zh: 但FBI几乎立刻就介入了。

sentences.en: And how does Hoover feel about that?
sentences.zh: 胡佛对此怎么看？

sentences.en: Really interesting this.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有意思。

sentences.en: So Hoover obviously despises King.
sentences.zh: 胡佛显然非常鄙视金博士。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing, Sir Hampton Sides in his book talks about this.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，汉普顿·赛兹爵士在书中提到了这一点。

sentences.en: It's the biggest manhunt in FBI history.
sentences.zh: 这是FBI历史上最大规模的搜捕行动。

sentences.en: Hoover had working on it 3,500 agents and they spent $200 million to track down King's killer.
sentences.zh: 胡佛动用了3500名探员，花费了2亿美元来追踪金博士的凶手。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing is the one thing Hoover cared about most of all, apart from a lot of very insalubrious things, was the reputation of the Bureau.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，除了那些见不得光的勾当，胡佛最在意的其实是FBI的声誉。

sentences.en: That meant more to him than anything.
sentences.zh: 这对他来说比什么都重要。

sentences.en: To capture King's assassin would be good for the FBI.
sentences.zh: 抓获金博士的刺客对FBI来说是件好事。

sentences.en: He will not be accused.
sentences.zh: 他不想被指责。

sentences.en: He does not want to be accused of having gone soft on this because of racism.
sentences.zh: 他不想因为种族主义的原因被指责在处理此事上软弱无能。

sentences.en: He wants to show the world that the FBI will crack this case.
sentences.zh: 他要向全世界证明FBI能破获此案。

sentences.en: We are the best in the world at doing this, no matter who the victim is.
sentences.zh: 无论受害者是谁，我们都是世界上处理此类案件最棒的。

sentences.en: So is Hoover's contempt for Martin Luther King, is that racist or political?
sentences.zh: 那么，胡佛对马丁·路德·金的蔑视，是出于种族主义还是政治原因？

sentences.en: Oh, I think both.
sentences.zh: 哦，我想两者皆有。

sentences.en: I think probably both.
sentences.zh: 我想大概两者都有。

sentences.en: I think a bit of both, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我觉得两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: I think the two are fused in Hoover's minds.
sentences.zh: 我认为在胡佛的脑海里，这两者是融合在一起的。

sentences.en: He regards the civil rights movement as a subversive, communist, all of this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他把民权运动视为颠覆性的、共产主义的，诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: And undoubtedly there's a racial dimension to that, but there's a kind of political ideological one as well, I would say.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，其中有种族因素，但我也认为还有一种政治意识形态的因素。

sentences.en: So I don't want to sound like a stuck record on these American assassinations, but as for the Kennedy assassination,
sentences.zh: 我不想在这些美国刺杀事件上显得像个复读机，但就肯尼迪遇刺案而言，

sentences.en: you could say the law enforcement authorities are actually really good.
sentences.zh: 你可以说执法部门其实非常高效。

sentences.en: Because within an hour, they know, or they're pretty sure the shot has come from room 5B, which was being occupied by a man called John Willard.
sentences.zh: 因为在一小时内，他们就知道，或者说非常确定枪声来自5B房间，而那个房间当时住着一个叫约翰·威拉德的人。

sentences.en: They've also found the weapon, which was left near the scene.
sentences.zh: 他们还在现场附近找到了凶器。

sentences.en: It's a Remington Game Master rifle, but Willard himself has completely vanished.
sentences.zh: 那是一把雷明顿Game Master步枪，但威拉德本人已经完全消失了。

sentences.en: He's nowhere to be seen.
sentences.zh: 不见踪影。

sentences.en: So this manhunt begins.
sentences.zh: 于是搜捕行动开始了。

sentences.en: They eventually work out that Willard is probably a man who's going by a series of other aliases.
sentences.zh: 他们最终查出威拉德很可能是一个使用多个化名的人。

sentences.en: The one he uses most is Eric Stavro Galt.
sentences.zh: 他最常用的一个是埃里克·斯塔夫罗·加尔特。
zh_words: 埃里克·斯塔夫罗·加尔特

sentences.en: I've never heard of a more obvious hewn.
sentences.zh: 我从没听过比这更明显的化名了。

sentences.en: Yeah, especially because this is clearly based on Ernst Stavro Blofeld.
sentences.zh: 是啊，尤其是这显然是基于恩斯特·斯塔夫罗·布洛菲尔德（Ernst Stavro Blofeld）的名字。
zh_words: 恩斯特·斯塔夫罗·布洛菲尔德

sentences.en: Galt, yeah.
sentences.zh: 加尔特，没错。

sentences.en: So they work out that this guy, Galt, has fled Memphis in a Ford Mustang.
sentences.zh: 他们查出这个叫加尔特的家伙开着一辆福特野马逃离了孟菲斯。

sentences.en: He drove to Atlanta and then he got a series of buses and he's ended up in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 他开车去了亚特兰大，然后换乘了几趟巴士，最后到了多伦多。

sentences.en: In Toronto, he hung around there for a considerable time.
sentences.zh: 在多伦多，他逗留了相当长一段时间。

sentences.en: He stole the identity of a policeman called Ramon George Snade.
sentences.zh: 他盗用了警察雷蒙·乔治·斯内德的身份。

sentences.en: I mean, that was actually really his name.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那其实真是他的名字。

sentences.en: It wasn't.
sentences.zh: 并不是。

sentences.en: And he flew to London.
sentences.zh: 然后他飞往伦敦。

sentences.en: And his dream was to go to Rhodesia, to the white supremacist colony that had broken away from Britain, declared independence unilaterally.
sentences.zh: 他的梦想是去罗得西亚，那个从英国分裂出来、单方面宣布独立的白人至上主义殖民地。

sentences.zh: 他曾参与过让华莱士进入加州选票的努力。

sentences.en: He also seems to have been stalking Martin Luther King for months.
sentences.zh: 他似乎还跟踪了马丁·路德·金好几个月。

sentences.en: This police found in his apartment in Los Angeles, they found a map of Atlanta with King's house and his church circled.

sentences.zh: 人们开始选择自己想触犯的法律，这基本上是里根暗示他不支持民权运动的方式，

sentences.en: hinting that he didn't approve of the civil rights movement, which I don't think, personally, I don't think reflects terribly well on Reagan.
sentences.zh: 我个人认为，这对他来说并不是什么光彩的事。

sentences.zh: 孟菲斯罢工在一周后在白宫的压力下得到解决，约翰逊白宫说，你们必须把这件事了结。

sentences.en: So the strikers basically got everything they wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以罢工者基本上得到了他们想要的一切。

sentences.en: Their campaign had worked.
sentences.zh: 他们的运动成功了。

sentences.en: But just as King's aides had predicted, the Poor People's Campaign, this kind of biblically inspired campaign that was his last great effort, was a complete and utter disaster.
sentences.zh: 但正如金博士的助手们所预料的那样，“穷人运动”——这场受圣经启发、作为他最后伟大努力的运动，完全是一场灾难。

sentences.en: It was incredibly badly organized.

sentences.en: The rebellions that have been occurring around this country are just light stuff compared with what's about to happen.

sentences.en: There is kind of fighting in the streets.
